config.question: Does bidirectional multi-positive alignment improve discrimination of minimally changed constraint records over BCE and pairwise ranking on identical data?
config.scope: Oracle-candidate retrieval diagnostic, not a complete compiler or new-method confirmation
config.source: frozen v6 train/dev only; sha256(group_id) selection; E/I/N stay grouped
config.encoder_mode: frozen base, FP32 CPU, mean last hidden state; no truncation
config.negative_policy: Same task candidate pool for all E/I/N. Mutate one bound, role, class or omission. Drop predicate-different candidates indistinguishable from any gold on the enumerated task domain; preserve witness for retained differences. Do not use other batches as automatic negatives.
config.positive_policy: Frozen normalized predicate-set equality, including duplicate/reordered predicates; E and I can share positives. Not general linguistic equivalence.
config.matching: Identical projections, initial state, sampled group sequence, encoder cache, candidate pools and update count per seed; only loss changes
config.analysis: Paired task-group bootstrap per fitted seed, descriptive only; show both seeds and all arms
config.gate: Proceed to an end-to-end binding experiment only if contrastive beats both BCE and rank by >=3pp predicate retrieval in each seed, with N false alarm no more than 1pp worse. Passing is screening evidence, not publication evidence.
config.stop: Nonfinite loss/gradient/parameter, hash mismatch, unsupported record, time budget, or no stable gain stops scaling. Never overwrite a failed run.
limitations: Gold-derived candidate pool makes this easier than free-form compilation
No held-out tool or template confirmation in this pilot
Frozen encoder probe cannot determine whether end-to-end contrastive finetuning would work
Finite execution-domain equivalence is not universal semantic equivalence
